children.value: This page is a transient heat-conduction model of one 2512 chip resistor on an FR4 coupon. The resistor solid is the KiCad library part

. The dissipation is 0.1 W, spread uniformly through that solid. Two 1 oz copper traces, each 20 mil wide and 1 inch long, leave the end caps. Salome 9.16 meshes the assembly. ElmerSolver 26.2 integrates the heat equation for 585 s. ParaView 5.10 draws the temperature, including a movie of the whole run.
The solid is one body from the KiCad 3D library, file

, header date 2018-01-04. KiCad StepUp wrote it in FreeCAD. The library is CC-BY-SA 4.0 with the KiCad library exception. Salome reads the STEP in metres. The mesh script scales it by 1000 and works in millimetres.

That outline matches the Vishay D/CRCW e3 CRCW2512 body in document 20035, revision 14-Apr-2026: length 6.3 ± 0.20 mm, width 3.15 ± 0.15 mm, height 0.6 ± 0.10 mm. The STEP width of 3.20 mm is inside the width tolerance. Vishay lists a 1.0 W rating at 70 °C and a film temperature of 155 °C. The construction is a cermet film and glass on high-grade alumina, with a nickel barrier and matte tin.

The STEP contains the outline only. The film, the glass, the nickel, and the tin are absent, so the 0.1 W fills the one solid the file does contain. That solid is given the conductivity of CoorsTek AD-96 96% alumina, 24.7 W/(m·K), from ASTM C408. CoorsTek also lists this grade as ADD-96. The density is 3720 kg/m³, from ASTM C20, and the specific heat is 880 J/(kg·K) at 100 °C, from ASTM E1269. Vishay calls the substrate high-grade alumina and does not name this grade. The tin terminations use the same values because they are part of the same solid.

The case file is the record of the materials, the source, the time steps, and the air boundary.

! Transient heat conduction for one 2512 chip on FR4.
! The chip solid is R_2512_6332Metric.step, scaled to metres by ElmerGrid.
! It is one body. The 0.1 W is uniform in that volume. There is no separate
! resistive film in the CAD file.
!
! Chip conductivity is 24.7 W/(m K), CoorsTek ADD-96 96% alumina, ASTM C408.
! The tin terminations are not a separate solid, so they use that same value.
! Copper is 401 W/(m K), pure copper near 300 K. The foil is 0.035 mm (1 oz).
! FR4 is 0.4 W/(m K) in every direction, the single Isola 370HR value from
! ASTM E1952. That test is through the thickness. The glass fabric is
! anisotropic; this case does not add an in-plane conductivity.
! Alumina density is 3720 kg/m^3 and specific heat is 880 J/(kg K)
! at 100 C, CoorsTek AD-96, ASTM C20 and ASTM E1269.
! Copper density is 8960 kg/m^3 and specific heat is 385 J/(kg K).
! Isola does not publish a 370HR density or specific heat. This case uses
! 1850 kg/m^3, the usual FR-4 specific gravity of 1.85, and
! 1000 J/(kg K). Those two numbers set how fast the board warms.
! They do not set the final temperature.
!
! Each trace is 20 mil wide and 1 inch long, measured from the outer end of
! the body. Under the part, the trace covers the bottom metal of that end cap
! and stays 20 mil wide. It does not widen into the Vishay land pattern.
! Open surfaces lose heat by a coefficient of 10 W/(m^2 K) to air at 25 C.
! That coefficient is a mid-range natural-convection value, not a measurement
! of this coupon.
!
! Chip volume 1.10970223e-08 m^3. Alumina density 3720.0 kg/m^3.
! Heat source 2.42242646e+03 W/kg. Product 0.100000 W.
! Steps: 10 20 24 intervals of 0.5 5.0 20.0 seconds. The last frame is at 585 s.

Header
  Mesh DB "." "mesh"
End

! ElmerGrid writes these $ names. They have to be included before the
! Body sections. The solver does not load mesh.names until after this file
! is parsed, so a bare "$ chip" is an unknown MATC name without this line.
Include "mesh/mesh.names"

Simulation
  Max Output Level = 4
  Coordinate System = Cartesian
  Simulation Type = Transient
  Timestepping Method = BDF
  BDF Order = 2
  Timestep Intervals(3) = 10 20 24
  Timestep Sizes(3) = 0.5 5.0 20.0
  Output Intervals(3) = 1 1 1
  Post File = case.vtu
End

Body 1
  Name = chip
  Target Bodies(1) = $ chip
  Equation = 1
  Material = 1
  Body Force = 1
  Initial Condition = 1
End

Body 2
  Name = copper_left
  Target Bodies(1) = $ copper_left
  Equation = 1
  Material = 2
  Initial Condition = 1
End

Body 3
  Name = copper_right
  Target Bodies(1) = $ copper_right
  Equation = 1
  Material = 2
  Initial Condition = 1
End

Body 4
  Name = fr4
  Target Bodies(1) = $ fr4
  Equation = 1
  Material = 3
  Initial Condition = 1
End

Solver 1
  Equation = Heat Equation
  Variable = Temperature
  Variable Dofs = 1
  Procedure = "HeatSolve" "HeatSolver"
  Linear System Solver = Iterative
  Linear System Iterative Method = BiCGStab
  Linear System Preconditioning = ILU1
  Linear System Max Iterations = 2000
  Linear System Convergence Tolerance = 1.0e-10
  Nonlinear System Max Iterations = 1
  Nonlinear System Convergence Tolerance = 1.0e-8
  Steady State Convergence Tolerance = 1.0e-8
End

Equation 1
  Name = Heat
  Active Solvers(1) = 1
End

! HeatSolve multiplies Heat Source by Density. The source is therefore
! W/kg, and Density * Heat Source * volume is the electrical power.
! The storage term is Density * Heat Capacity * dT/dt.
Material 1
  Name = alumina
  Heat Conductivity = 24.7
  Density = 3720.0
  Heat Capacity = 880.0
End

Material 2
  Name = copper
  Heat Conductivity = 401.0
  Density = 8960.0
  Heat Capacity = 385.0
End

Material 3
  Name = fr4
  Heat Conductivity = 0.4
  Density = 1850.0
  Heat Capacity = 1000.0
End

Body Force 1
  Name = chip_power
  Heat Source = 2.42242646e+03
End

Initial Condition 1
  Name = ambient
  Temperature = 25.0
End

Boundary Condition 1
  Name = air
  Target Boundaries(1) = $ air
  Heat Transfer Coefficient = 10.0
  External Temperature = 25.0
End

At 0.5 s the field runs from 25.00 °C to 26.30 °C. The hottest node is 34.97 °C at 5 s, 48.45 °C at 30 s, 51.31 °C at 60 s, and 53.24 °C at 105 s. At 585 s the field runs from 25.72 °C to 56.53 °C. The color scale on every frame, and on both stills, is locked from 25.00 °C to 56.53 °C. No earlier frame is hotter than the last.
Over the last 20 s the hottest node rose from 56.524 °C to 56.534 °C. The solver norm changed by 0.009 on that step, a relative change of

children.html: 2.7×10−42.7\times 10^{-4}2.7×10−4

children.value: . The chip has leveled, and the coupon is still creeping. A rise of 31.53 K at 0.1 W is about 315 K/W for this mounting. The temperature drop sits at the two contacts, 0.2438 mm² each, where the heat enters the 20 mil traces, and then in the FR4. The 56.53 °C peak is the one-fifth scaling of the earlier steady peak, 182.953 °C, on this same mesh.

56.53 °C is the hottest node in this mesh at 585 s. Vishay’s film limit is 155 °C on the 1 W test. This page uses 0.1 W, 20 mil traces, a coupon of about 61 mm by 13 mm, and a convection coefficient of 10 W/(m²·K). The film is absent from the STEP. The temperature belongs to this model.
The clip is 54 frames at 5 frames per second, so it runs 10.8 s. The first 10 frames are 0.5 s apart, the next 20 are 5 s apart, and the last 24 are 20 s apart. The clock is the simulation time.
